schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE EMPLOYEE (
    EMPID INT,
    NAME VARCHAR(255),
    SUPERVISOR INT,
    SALARY INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (EMPID),
    CHECK (EMPID <> SUPERVISOR),
    CHECK (SALARY >= 0)
);

CREATE TABLE BONUS (
    EMPID INT,
    BONUS INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (EMPID),
    FOREIGN KEY (EMPID) REFERENCES EMPLOYEE(EMPID),
    CHECK (BONUS >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT EMPLOYEE.NAME, BONUS.BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE BONUS < 1000 OR BONUS IS NULL
q2: SELECT NAME, BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE IFNULL(BONUS, 0)<1000
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMPLOYEE.NAME, BONUS.BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE BONUS < 1000 OR BONUS IS NULL
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT NAME, BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE IFNULL(BONUS, 0)<1000
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. Both queries return all employees from EMPLOYEE, joining with BONUS on EMPID. Q1 uses a WHERE clause with BONUS < 1000 OR BONUS IS NULL, which includes all rows since LEFT JOIN ensures no loss of EMPLOYEE rows. Q2 uses IFNULL(BONUS, 0) < 1000, which also includes all rows because replacing NULL with 0 still satisfies 0 < 1000. Therefore, the result sets will be the same.
